category_title: Second-grade Hispanic students who rely on graphophonic cues but struggle with semantic monitoring
minimal_context: The student is reading the book Amelia Bedelia and the Baby aloud during a one-on-one tutoring session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start reading this book, Amelia Bedelia and the Baby.

STUDENT: Okay. I want to read it, but I don't think I know enough words.

TUTOR: Just try your best. Go ahead and read the sentence on this page.

STUDENT: Babies should have...

TUTOR: What is the last word in that sentence?

STUDENT: (Looks at the picture) ...bowls. Babies should have bowls.

options.A: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall additional factual information about the book's characters, setting, or plot.
options.B: Ask follow-up questions throughout the one-on-one reading session to model conversational skills for the student.
options.C: Emphasize mastery goal orientation during the session by highlighting the value of engagement for pursuing deep learning and reading improvement.
options.D: Teach a placeholder strategy of reading the first letter of a word instead of the entire word as long as meaning is maintained.
